question.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
question.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $2.$ Therefore,
$\omega =2.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =2$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[4(D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4(C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)]+4t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) & =-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 4D\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4C\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & =-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{7}{4}$ and $D=0.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

Only solutions I and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
